messages.subject: object 'ReorderModel' not found
messages.body_plain:
I am running the following script to familiarize myself with GenomicSEM. I am unable to execute the commonfactor command and receive the error that the ReorderModel object cannot be found. I appreciate any suggestions to get around this. Thank you!

ldsc_out <- ldsc(traits =c("ADHD.sumstats.gz","AlcDep.sumstats.gz","Anorexia.sumstats.gz",
                            "Anxiety.sumstats.gz","Autism.sumstats.gz"),
                  trait.names= c("adhd","alcdep","anorexia","anxiety","autism"),
                  ld = "eur_w_ld_chr/", wld="eur_w_ld_chr/",
                  sample.prev = NA,
                  population.prev = NA)

k<-nrow(ldsc_out$S)
SE<-matrix(0, k, k)
SE[lower.tri(SE,diag=TRUE)] <-sqrt(diag(ldsc_out$V))

DWLS<- commonfactor(ldsc_out,estimation="DWLS")
ML<- commonfactor(ldsc_out,estimation="ML")

messages.subject: Missing data
messages.body_plain:
Dear Andrew,

I am going through Genomic SEM Tutorial. I was wondering whether Genomic SEM could handle missing data, for example, some individuals may miss a few phenotype data in some traits?

Thank you and all the best
Tianhua
messages.body_snippet:
Dear Andrew,

I am going through Genomic SEM Tutorial. I was wondering whether Genomic SEM could handle missing data, for example, some individuals may miss a few phenotype data in some traits?

Thank

messages.subject: Re: Missing data
messages.body_plain:
Hi Tianhua,

Thanks for your question! Genomic SEM does allow for individuals to be missing data on some traits, and since the package uses only univariate GWAS summary statistics as input it can handle phenotypes for which the participant samples are completely non-overlapping. For example, if you have GWAS summary statistics for trait X, you can examine the genetic correlation with GWAS summary statistics for trait Y even if none of the participants from the trait X GWAS participated in the trait Y GWAS. That, in my mind, is one of the best things about Genomic SEM is that it allows you to model the genetic correlation among traits that you may never have in the same sample (e.g., two very rare traits). The package does not require you to know ahead of time the level or amount of sample overlap across summary statistics as it automatically corrects for this. Hope this helps and let me know if you have any other questions!

Best,
  Andrew

messages.subject: Re: object 'ReorderModel' not found
messages.body_plain:
Just an update for the general group; the issue was that lavaan package, which Genomic SEM uses to estimate models, posted a package update on July 3rd, 2019 that was causing some mild incompatibility issues. Genomic SEM was appropriately updated and this model is now running. Thanks again Frank for brining this to our attention!

-Andrew
